title: "Nested Subqueries"
number-depth: 2

A **subquery** is simply a `select-from-where` block placed *inside* another query. SQL lets you nest subqueries in the `WHERE`, `FROM`, and `SELECT` clauses.

- `select`  :  Must return a single scalar value.
- `from`  :  Can return any valid relation (table).
- `where`  :  Used in expressions like `Attribute <operation> (subquery)`.

```{=html}
<div class="flow"><div class="box"><b>where</b><span>Attribute &lt;operation&gt; (subquery)</span></div><div class="box"><b>from</b><span>any valid relation (table)</span></div><div class="box"><b>select</b><span>a single scalar value</span></div></div>
```

All examples on this page run on the course datasets: press **Run** on any query to see its result.

---

## Subqueries in the `WHERE` Clause

Typically used to test **set membership**, **set comparison**, and **set cardinality**.

### Set Membership: `IN` / `NOT IN`

*Example:* Find courses offered in Fall 2009 **and** in Spring 2008.

```{.sql db="university"}
select distinct course_id
from section
where semester = 'Fall' and year = 2009 and
      course_id in (select course_id
                    from section
                    where semester = 'Spring' and year = 2008);
```

> Swap `in` for `not in` to find courses offered in Fall 2009 **but not** in Spring 2008.

### Set Comparison: `SOME` and `ALL`

| Clause | Meaning | Logic |
|---|---|---|
| **`some`** | True if comparison holds for **at least one** row in subquery | $\exists\, t \in r : F \langle\text{comp}\rangle\, t$ |
| **`all`** | True if comparison holds for **every** row in subquery | $\forall\, t \in r : F \langle\text{comp}\rangle\, t$ |

::: {.callout-note title="Note"}
\<comp\> can be: <, ≤, >, ≥, =, ≠
:::

*Example:* Instructors earning more than **some** instructor in Biology:

```{.sql db="university"}
select name, salary
from instructor
where salary > some (select salary
                     from instructor
                     where dept_name = 'Biology');
```

*Example:* Instructors earning more than **all** instructors in Biology:

```{.sql db="university"}
select name, salary
from instructor
where salary > all (select salary
                    from instructor
                    where dept_name = 'Biology');
```

**How the result is decided.** Biology has two salaries: 45538.32 and 77036.18.

```{=html}
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>Instructor</th><th>salary</th><th>&gt; some</th><th>&gt; all</th></tr><tr><td>Gutierrez</td><td>45310.53</td><td>✗</td><td>✗</td></tr><tr><td>Murata</td><td>61387.56</td><td>✓ (beats 45538.32)</td><td>✗</td></tr><tr><td>Romero</td><td>79070.08</td><td>✓</td><td>✓ (beats both)</td></tr></table></div>
```

### Test for Empty Sets: `EXISTS`

- `exists r` is true if `r` is non-empty.
- `not exists r` is true if `r` is empty.

*Example:* Find courses offered in both Fall 2009 and Spring 2008, using a **correlated subquery** (inner query refers to the outer query's variable).

```{.sql db="university"}
select course_id
from section as S
where semester = 'Fall' and year = 2009 and
      exists (select *
              from section as T
              where semester = 'Spring' and year = 2008
                    and S.course_id = T.course_id);
```

- `S` is the **correlation name** (outer query variable)
- The inner query referencing `S` is the **correlated subquery**

```{=html}
<div class="flow steps"><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>take a row S</b></div><span>a Fall 2009 section</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>run the subquery</b></div><span>Spring 2008 rows with the same course_id</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>non-empty?</b></div><span>exists is true: keep S</span></div></div>
```

*Example:* Find teams that have played against **all** other teams (uses `not exists` + set difference logic):

```{.sql db="flis"}
select t.name
from teams as t
where not exists (
    (select team_id from teams where team_id <> t.team_id)
    except
    (select guest_team_id from matches where host_team_id = t.team_id
     union
     select host_team_id from matches where guest_team_id = t.team_id)
);
```

For each team, "all other teams" **minus** "teams it has played" must be empty:

```{=html}
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>Team</th><th>Other teams not yet played</th><th>Kept?</th></tr><tr><td>Amigos</td><td>none (empty)</td><td>✓</td></tr><tr><td>Thunder</td><td>Rainbow</td><td>✗</td></tr><tr><td>Rainbow</td><td>Thunder, All Stars, Arawali</td><td>✗</td></tr></table></div>
```

### Test for Duplicates: `UNIQUE`

`unique (subquery)` is true if the subquery's result has **no duplicate rows**.

```sql
select t.name
from teams as t
where unique (select m.host_team_id
              from matches as m
              where m.host_team_id = t.team_id);
```
*(Finds teams that hosted at most one match.)*

::: {.callout-note title="Note"}
PostgreSQL does not implement `unique`. The same query, written with a count, runs on the dataset:
:::

```{.sql db="flis"}
select t.name
from teams as t
where (select count(*)
       from matches as m
       where m.host_team_id = t.team_id) <= 1;
```

## Subqueries in the FROM Clause

A subquery can stand in for a table, letting you filter on an **aggregate** without `HAVING`.

*Example:* Average salary of departments where average salary exceeds 90,000:

```{.sql db="university"}
select dept_name, avg_salary
from (select dept_name, round(avg(salary), 2) as avg_salary
      from instructor
      group by dept_name) as dept_avg
where avg_salary > 90000;
```

```{=html}
<div class="flow steps"><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>inner query</b></div><span>one row per department</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>as dept_avg</b></div><span>name the result</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>outer where</b></div><span>keep avg_salary &gt; 90000</span></div></div>
```

### The `WITH` Clause

`with` defines a **temporary, named result** (like a scratchpad table) visible only to the query that follows.

*Example:* Find the name of the department that has the maximum budget.

```{.sql db="university"}
with max_budget(value) as
    (select max(budget) from department)
select department.dept_name
from department, max_budget
where department.budget = max_budget.value;
```

Multiple `with` blocks can be chained for multi-step logic:

*Example:* Find the names of the departments whose total salary expense is greater than the average total salary expense across all departments.

```{=html}
<div class="flow steps"><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>dept_total</b></div><span>total salary per department</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>dept_total_avg</b></div><span>average of those totals</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>final select</b></div><span>departments above the average</span></div></div>
```

```{.sql db="university"}
with dept_total(dept_name, value) as
    (select dept_name, sum(salary)
     from instructor
     group by dept_name),
dept_total_avg(value) as
    (select avg(value) from dept_total)
select dept_name
from dept_total, dept_total_avg
where dept_total.value > dept_total_avg.value;
```

## Subqueries in the SELECT Clause

A **scalar subquery** returns exactly one value, used wherever a single value is expected.

```{.sql db="university"}
select dept_name,
       (select count(*)
        from instructor
        where department.dept_name = instructor.dept_name) as num_instructors
from department;
```

::: {.callout-note title="Note"}
If the subquery returns more than one row, this causes a **runtime error**.
:::

## Modifying the Database

```{=html}
<div class="flow"><div class="box grey"><b>Database modification</b><span>delete · insert · update</span></div><div class="box"><b>DELETE</b><span>remove tuples</span></div><div class="box"><b>INSERT</b><span>add tuples</span></div><div class="box"><b>UPDATE</b><span>change values</span></div></div>
```

These statements change the dataset. Each example is wrapped in `begin; … rollback;` so the data is restored after you run it.

### Deletion

```{.sql db="university"}
begin;
-- Delete all instructors
delete from instructor;

-- Delete instructors from one department
delete from instructor where dept_name = 'Finance';

-- Delete instructors in departments located in a specific building
delete from instructor
where dept_name in (select dept_name
                    from department
                    where building = 'Taylor');
rollback;
```

**Tricky case:** Delete instructors earning less than the average salary.

```{.sql db="university"}
begin;
delete from instructor
where salary < (select avg(salary) from instructor);
select count(*) from instructor;
rollback;
```

::: {.callout-note title="Note"}
As rows are deleted, the average changes! Solution: **(1)** computing the average and identifying all rows to delete *first*, then **(2)** deleting them — without recomputing mid-way.
:::

```{=html}
<div class="flow steps"><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>phase 1</b></div><span>compute the average once</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>phase 1</b></div><span>mark every row below it</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>phase 2</b></div><span>delete the marked rows</span></div></div>
```

### Insertion

```{.sql db="university"}
begin;
insert into course
values ('CS-437', 'Database Systems', 'Comp. Sci.', 4);

-- with tot_cred set to null
insert into student
values ('3003', 'Green', 'Finance', null);

-- insert from another query's results
insert into student
select id, name, dept_name, 0
from instructor
where id not in (select id from student);
rollback;
```

::: {.callout-note title="Note"}
The entire `select-from-where` is evaluated **before** any row is inserted — otherwise `insert into table1 select * from table1` would loop infinitely.
:::

### Updates

**Conditional updates** — give a 3% raise above 100,000, 5% below (order matters!):

```{.sql db="university"}
begin;
update instructor set salary = salary * 1.03 where salary > 100000;
update instructor set salary = salary * 1.05 where salary <= 100000;
rollback;
```

Cleaner with a **`case`** statement (single pass, no ordering issues):

```{.sql db="university"}
begin;
update instructor
set salary = case
    when salary <= 100000 then salary * 1.05
    else salary * 1.03
end;
rollback;
```

**Updates with scalar subqueries** — recompute total credits per student:

```{.sql db="university"}
begin;
update student S
set tot_cred = (select sum(credits)
                from takes, course
                where takes.course_id = course.course_id and
                      S.id = takes.id and
                      takes.grade <> 'F' and
                      takes.grade is not null);
rollback;
```
*(Find the total credits earned by each student (excluding failed or uncollected grades) and update their record in the student table.)*
